transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
Lately I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just disappeared, and those thoughts are starting to scare me. I've just felt so completely overwhelmed and I didn't know where else to go.
Have you had a similar episode of depression or anxiety like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, this isn't the first time. I've been cycling between really intense highs and these crushing, dark lows since the year after my divorce, which was about a year ago. This current dark stretch has been going on for about a month now without letting up.
Have you had one or more similar depressive episodes before this current one, with periods of feeling back to your usual self in between?

Yes, I've been through these dark crashes before. Since my divorce about a year ago, I've been cycling between those intense highs and these deep lows, with only brief periods in between where things leveled out for a bit.

During those 'really intense highs,' did you have a period of at least several days where you needed much less sleep, felt unusually energized or confident, talked more than usual, or did risky things?

Yes, during those highs over the past year, I would sleep maybe three hours a night and wake up feeling completely wired. I honestly felt like a visionary genius who was the only one who could fix the city's transport system, so I took on tons of extra projects, started a blog, and swiped on dating apps because I just couldn't sit still.
During those high periods, did you ever hear or see things other people couldn’t, or become so convinced of something unusual that others said it was not true?
No, I've never seen or heard things that weren't actually there, even during my highest periods. I also haven't held any beliefs that others found completely unreal.
Have those high-energy periods ever lasted at least 4 days in a row, or did they last a week or more and cause major problems at work, with money, or in relationships?

Yes, those high-energy periods lasted for weeks at a time and caused major disruptions in my life. I would work through the night and overcommit, which eventually led to my manager quietly removing me from client presentations and me missing critical deadlines. It also strained my relationships because I'd swing from being giddy to incredibly irritable and snappy with my colleagues and family.
During your low periods, do you feel depressed or lose interest/pleasure in things most of the day nearly every day for at least 2 weeks at a time?

Yes, during these low periods, it feels like someone has turned the color down on my life and I lose all interest in things I used to love, like my work projects and weekend hiking. This current dark stretch has been going on continuously for about a month now without letting up.
When you think about disappearing, have you had any intention to act on those thoughts or made any plan to hurt yourself?

Yes, several times a day I catch myself planning out quiet ways to die, like picturing driving off the bridge I helped design or stockpiling my old pain pills, and it really scares me. I just keep thinking that everyone, including my parents and my ex, would probably be relieved not to have to worry about me anymore.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable and you had much more energy than usual, with little need for sleep, and it caused major problems or led to hospitalization?

Yes, since my divorce last year, I've had high periods lasting weeks where I felt giddy, invincible, or highly irritable, buzzing with energy on only three hours of sleep. It caused major problems at work, and my manager had to quietly remove me from client-facing presentations because of my volatile behavior and missed deadlines, though I have never been hospitalized.
During those high periods, did you ever need to be hospitalized, or did you become so out of control that you could not function safely at work, at home, or in your relationships?

No, I was never hospitalized during those high periods because I felt invincible and didn't think anything was wrong at the time. Looking back, though, I was definitely disrupting things by snapping at coworkers, slamming doors in meetings, and staying up all night, which is why my manager took me off client presentations. The urgent psychiatric assessment only happened recently, after I crashed into this current severe depression.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or active than usual, even if it did not cause major problems?

Yes, those high-energy periods have cycled on and off for at least the past year since my divorce. During those phases, I felt completely invincible and buzzed with energy on just three hours of sleep, working through the night while my mind jumped all over the place and I snapped at my coworkers.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least 4 days where you felt unusually energetic or irritable with much less need for sleep, but it was not severe enough to cause major work or relationship problems?

No, those high periods actually did cause major problems for me. When I felt that wired and only slept about three hours, I would snap at coworkers and overcommit my team. It was disruptive enough that my manager had to take me off client-facing presentations entirely.

Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days when you felt abnormally energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, and did it clearly cause major problems at work, at home, or in relationships?

Yes, a couple of months ago I had a stretch lasting several weeks where I felt completely wired and buzzed with energy on only three hours of sleep. I would swing from feeling invincible to extremely irritable, snapping at coworkers and slamming doors in meetings. It caused major problems at work, leading my manager to quietly take me off client-facing presentations.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of abnormally elevated/irritable mood with markedly decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity, pressured overactivity, and clear functional impairment lasting weeks, alternating with prolonged depressive episodes with anhedonia and suicidal ideation. This pattern is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, currently depressed, with history of manic episodes (bipolar I disorder). No psychotic symptoms were reported.
